text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
American founder of the Christian Science Movement, MARY BAKER EDDY, was born in 1821.
Norwegian explorer, ROALD AMUNDSEN, who was the first to reach the South Pole, was born in 1872.
American actress, BARBARA STANWYCK, who starred in a long list of films, was born in 1907.

Australian cricketer, STAN McCABE, who was a successful batsman against bodyline bowling in the 1932 test series against England, was born in 1910. He died in a cliff fall while trying to dispose of a dead possum.
American actress and dancer, GINGER ROGERS, who partnered FRED ASTAIRE in ten musicals, was born in 1911.
Australian tennis player, MARGARET COURT, who won the Grand Slam in 1970, was born in 1942.
Australian jazz and blues singer, MARGARET ROADKNIGHT, was born in 1943.
American drummer and songwriter, STEWART COPELAND, who was co-founder of the band Police, was born in 1952.
** EVENTS **
622 : The Islamic Era began when MOHAMMED began the Hejira. his flight from Mecca to Medina.
1439 : Kissing was banned in England in an attempt to
stop the spread of germs.
1885 : French chemist and microbiologist LOUIS PASTEUR
reported success with his vaccine against rabies. The nine-year-old sufferer he treated made a rapid recovery after receiving a weakened strain of the virus.
1893 : More than 200 Australians set sail for Paraguay on
the "Royal Tar" on a quest to set up a New Australia as a utopian co-operative settlement. The South American venture failed but descendants of some of the colonists still live there.
1917 : The Bolsheviks began an attempt to seize power in
Petrograd but were defeated. TROTSKY was arrested and LENIN went into hiding.
1918 : The royal family of Russia, the Czar NICHOLAS II,
the Czarina ALEXANDRA, their children and members of their household staff were murdered by Bolsheviks at Yekaterinburg during the Russian revolution.
1935 : The world's first parking meters were installed in
Oklahoma city.
1945 : The first atomic bomb tests took place in the New

Mexico desert. Three weeks later, the Japanese city of Hiroshima became the real target for the new weapon. The city was destroyed by the atomic bomb on the 6th of August 1945, and three days later the city of Nagasaki was wiped out by the bomb.
1950 : The largest ever crowd to watch a soccer match,
over 199,000, saw Uruguay beat Brazil 2-1 in the World Cup final.
1969 : "Apollo II" carrying American astronauts NEIL
ARMSTRONG and EDWIN "BUZZ" ALDRIN was launched at Cape Kennedy. Five days later ARMSTRONG became the first man to set foot on the moon.
1972 : Queenslander JEFF LEWRY created a world record by
throwing a boomerang that travelled 82 metres.
1981 : American singer/songwriter HARRY CHAPIN died when
a truck drove into the back of his car. CHAPIN had a heart attack.
1982 : Australian Opposition leader, Labor's BILL HAYDEN,
survived a leadership challenge from BOB HAWKE. The vote was 42 to 37.
1986 : An underground explosion at the Moura coal-mine in
Queensland killed 12 miners.
1990 : At least 100 people died in a massive earthquake
in the Philippines.
1993 : Britain's MI5 security service ended more than 80
years of secrecy when it published a booklet on its operations.
1994 : The first fragments of the Shoemaker-Levy 9 comet
hit Jupiter.
1996 : GERMANO MACCARI was convicted of being one of two
killers who shot former Italian Prime Minister ALDO MORO in 1978.
